prompt: Can you build the CSV quoting function one case at a time? Before writing each bit of implementation, run a new automated check and confirm it fails. Once it passes, do the cleanup phase before starting the next case.

In the existing mesh exporter, rename the internal function go to writeFaceIndices and update its call sites. This is just to make the code understandable; the exported bytes, errors, and all other behavior must stay identical.

The transaction object needs a clear division of responsibilities: the caller must have an open transaction before commit, commit must leave a durable record when it succeeds, and all public operations must preserve the relationship between its phase and pending writes. Specify and check those rules.

We can afford one extra CI shard. Configure it to deliberately replace production functions with faulty implementations, exercise those changes with our test suite, and compute the fraction of injected faults the tests detect. Break that score down by module and attach it to the pull-request summary so we can prioritize weakly checked code.

The conservation staff and developers mean different things by 'specimen'. Facilitate an agreement about that domain concept and make the model, requirement documents, code, and our conversations with the staff use the agreed meaning. This task defines the vocabulary for new work; don't modify existing code.

For the rational-number library, generate supported numerator and nonzero-denominator pairs and check that reducing a fraction never changes its value and that a second reduction does nothing. Report a failing fraction if either rule breaks.

The proposed backup-service patch mixes a storage redesign with resumable uploads. Split it into two changes: first replace the existing subclass inheritance with a composed storage adapter, keeping every existing command, result, and failure unchanged. Then implement resumable uploads in small increments, running a new automated test to demonstrate the missing behavior before each production edit. Get that test passing and finish the cleanup phase before tackling the next increment.

For reserveSeats(), spell out the caller's required available capacity, the seats promised on success, and the seating-map consistency that all operations preserve. Then generate valid seating maps and request counts to check that every successful reservation satisfies those promises and keeps the map consistent.

Our polygon-area tests should check translation leaves area unchanged over generated valid polygons. After that, deliberately drop terms or flip signs in the area implementation and run the tests to find which of those injected faults they miss.

The librarians distinguish a title from a physical copy, but our current types blur them. Agree with the librarians on precise meanings, carry those words into requirements and model discussions, and rename the existing internal types accordingly without changing borrowing decisions or any other behavior.

Start the path normalizer with an automated check that currently fails, implement enough to satisfy it, then finish the cleanup phase before another increment. Use generated supported paths to check the general rule that normalizing a normalized path leaves it unchanged.

For attachChild(), document the caller's duty to supply an unattached node, the parent's new child relationship promised on success, and the tree consistency maintained across all methods. Enforce those obligations, and evaluate the tests by intentionally breaking the production attachment logic in small ways and seeing which introduced defects survive.

Before building the new harvest-lot service, have the growers and developers agree on what 'lot' and 'yield' mean in requirements, model discussions, and the code we'll write. Build each increment with a failing automated check first, make it pass, and do the cleanup phase before moving on. Finally, deliberately introduce small faults in that service implementation and find which faults its tests fail to catch.

Work with the racing officials and developers to agree on 'entrant' and 'classification' across the model, requirements, and code. Rename the existing internal classes to those agreed terms while preserving race results and every other behavior. Also make explicit the caller's obligations before classify(), its promised result afterward, and the object-state relationships every operation must maintain; adding those checks must not change behavior for existing valid callers.
Please use red-green-refactor to build the settings parser. Start with a failing automated test, implement enough for it to pass, and complete the cleanup stage before taking the next case.

The report-builder refactoring proposal still keeps column names and widths in separate arrays. Revise and implement that proposal using a single record per column so a later column change has one place to edit. The existing API, report format, and invalid-width behavior are fixed; this is a change to the current implementation's internal representation.

Apply DBC to the byte reader: callers must request no more than the remaining bytes, successful reads must advance the offset by the returned length, and every operation must maintain the offset within the buffer bounds.
Set up mutation testing for the permission evaluator, using deliberate production-code changes and our existing tests to find surviving faults.

Use a ubiquitous language for the new water-rights model. The water managers and developers should agree on what an allocation and a withdrawal mean and use those meanings in model discussions, requirements, and code. Existing implementation changes aren't part of this task.
Write a property-based test for the vector rotation function, generating finite supported vectors and angles and checking that rotation preserves vector length within the numerical tolerance.

Keep using TDD for the new compression mode. Independently of that workflow, the existing header reader has a variable named z; change that internal name and all its references to headerLength for clarity, with no changes to parsing or errors.

This is a refactoring of the existing auction code, not a behavior change. With the auctioneers, settle exactly what 'bid' and 'offer' mean, and make those shared meanings consistent in model discussions, requirements, and the internal code names as we restructure it.

Use design by contract for the matrix API. Add tests that generate conformable matrix pairs and verify generally that transposing their product equals multiplying their transposes in reverse order, allowing for the agreed floating-point tolerance.

Leave mutation testing enabled on the router package. Build the new route-alias feature through small increments: prove a new automated test fails first, implement until it passes, then complete the cleanup stage before starting another increment.

We're keeping the ubiquitous language agreed with the event organizers. For the registration object, write down the caller's responsibilities before confirm(), what a successful confirmation guarantees, and the relationship between capacity and confirmed registrations that must hold across all operations.

The queue already has property-based tests. Now assess whether that suite detects real mistakes: create temporary copies of the production queue code with comparisons reversed or updates omitted, run the tests on each, and report the faults that went unnoticed.

For the troubleshooting page, answer 'What does TTL mean in the cache settings, and which unit does expiry accept?' using the current API documentation. Add a cross-link to the existing configuration reference. This ticket changes documentation only.
Check that the uploaded avatar is below the size limit at the HTTP boundary. Return the existing 413 response for anything too large; otherwise keep the request handling as it is.

Our load harness fills valid request bodies from a seeded generator, and its CSV records payload size, worker count, and latency. Turn the completed run into a pivot table of median and p95 latency by payload-size bucket and worker count so we can decide where to profile next. Use the recorded measurements; there's no need to rerun the job.

The demo dataset must no longer show obsolete contact details. Write a one-off SQL script that overwrites the email column for archived demo accounts with placeholder addresses. Include a count-only preview and put the updates inside a transaction; leave the application code and schema untouched.
Take these eight handpicked protocol messages, edit one field in each test input, and assert the specified error for each edited example. The fixture file is the only thing that needs to change.

The disk reporter shows kilobytes where the spec requires kibibytes. Correct the calculation so the displayed numbers change. Leave the internal organization and names alone; I want the observable bug fixed.
The barcode reader is implemented and shipping. Add six example-based tests now, after the implementation, without changing or restructuring that implementation.
The old minutes say 'TDD was proposed and rejected'. Add that historical fact to the project timeline. Today's task is only documentation; don't adopt that approach or work on code or tests.
Do not introduce mutation testing or property-based testing here. Add only the three specified examples for accepting or rejecting a file extension, and leave the production code untouched.
Let's go with the approach we discussed earlier. Can you finish it?

For the changelog, describe the internal function renames that were completed in the last release and kept behavior unchanged. No further code changes are requested. Don't turn this historical summary into a new implementation task.

The old design document mentioned 'ubiquitous language', but we aren't adopting it in this task. Add a future coding-style note requiring an underscore prefix on private fields. This is documentation only, not existing code changes or shared domain terminology.

For a demonstration of weak assertions, disable selected assertions in copies of the tests and show how their checks disappear. Keep every byte of production code unchanged; we're not introducing production faults to assess the suite.

The retired plan said 'design by contract'. We're not reinstating it. Today add a standalone null check to the request boundary and time the endpoint over generated valid requests. The load run should record latency only.
